messages:
maria: hey team — posted a pic of my WFH corner, my ceramic fishtank is on the desk and it's making this weird hollow echo on calls, anyone seen this? (pic: https://imgur.com/a/ceramic-tank) :fish:
kevin: omg the fish are judging your background :laughing:
sam: science note: a shallow ceramic tank can act like a resonant cavity. mic placement helps — try moving the mic to the side of the tank, not between monitor+tank.
anya: also try a small foam shield behind the mic. cheap ones from amazon work wonders and fold up for storage.
maria: moved the mic, still some slapback when i raise my voice. Zoom's 'suppress background noise' on low doesn't catch it.
kevin: try enabling echo cancellation: Zoom > Settings > Audio > Advanced > check "Suppress persistent background noise" and "Echo cancellation". sometimes those are under the caret next to the mic selector.
maria: where is that on mac? zoom hides everything under mini-menus :sob:
sam: on mac: System Settings > Sound > Input to pick your device, then in Zoom click the ^ next to the mic, Audio Settings > Advanced. if you use an external usb mic try switching sample rate to 48k in the app.
anya: quick hack that worked for me: put a thin rubber mat or folded dish towel under the tank to decouple vibrations from the desk. solved a similar rattle from a speaker.
maria: tried the towel — immediate improvement! still a faint hollow reverb though. i also noticed when i set my phone on the tank lid to read notes, my bluetooth keyboard disconnects. interference?
sam: could be RF coupling with the tank lid (metal hinges?) or just your keyboard hopping channels. if you're on linux, these commands help inspect audio/input devices:
```
arecord -l
pactl list short sources
```
kevin: or, for a non-tech fix: small potted fern behind the tank breaks reflections and looks good. plant + towel = acoustic sculptures :thumbsup:
dev-bot: FYI — IT: Remember to register any company-issued peripherals with IT for warranty/replacement. (automated reminder)
maria: thanks all — trying towel + mic shield tomorrow AM and will report back with before/after audio clip. appreciate the tips! :pray:
